entries.note: PMID 9399943 abstract carries the 20%/50% BrdU sentence verbatim. 5/6-Nx rat, NPS R-568 (product_in_model false correct). EMA EPAR pharmacology names 5/6 Nx, so model_filed true holds.

Block 2004 abstract: -43% vs +9% PTH verbatim. Comparison is drafter's juxtaposition of Nemeth 2004 rat with patients (comparison_stated false, as in cf-cftr house style). NCT00037635/NCT00527267 have no results posted; registry_date null correct.
Nemeth 2004 (PMID 14593085) abstract carries the linear-PK 1-36 mg/kg sentence verbatim; epub 2003-10-30, print vol 308(2) 2004. untested is right: no patient exposure target stated.

Quote verbatim (EPAR p.14; near-duplicate p.36). But it is a toxicology safety-margin statement: toxic animal exposure ~ clinical exposure. No model-derived efficacious exposure target was tested; human dose came from PTH titration. Not a dose comparison. Also EMA is outside rule-1 whitelist. magnitude -> null.

Wada 1997 closing sentence verbatim. Rat prediction is hyperplasia suppression; Kawata 2008 (PMID 18813289) later adds aortic/cardiac calcification suppression and explicitly extrapolates to patients.
43% vs 5% primary endpoint verbatim; Ca x P -15% also in abstract. FDA label pools three studies as 40% vs 5%, not a conflict. Same PTH readout serves engagement and efficacy; see rule question 4.

HR 0.93 (0.85-1.02), P=0.11 and registry 2014-01-22 all confirmed. But EVOLVE tested death/CV events, which the rat never modelled; the rat's actual prediction (Kawata 2008 calcification) was tested by ADVANCE 2011: direction matched, primary P=0.073, volume CAC P=0.009. Not contra. No status change, so fold into entry 2; source_calls_it -> null (EVOLVE never mentions the rat).
Nemeth 2004 dose-dependent PTH/ionised-Ca sentence verbatim. EMA EPAR confirms dog 'Emesis, reduction in ionised calcium', monkey 'sporadic emesis', one-month dog 'frequent emesis'.

66%/25% sentence verbatim in the 2004 label; nausea 31/19, vomiting 27/15 in its AE table. EMA EPAR: 'hypocalcaemia ... was the dose-limiting toxicity in most species' verbatim; 2 consecutive Ca <7.5 mg/dL 5% vs <1%. Label itself has no animal hypocalcaemia statement, so comparison_stated false is right.

missing: Dose: I found no published rat-PD-exposure vs patient-exposure comparison either; the FDA NDA 21-688 clinical pharmacology review (accessdata.fda.gov) was not checked within budget and is the one place a genuine exposure-target comparison might exist.

Efficacy: the closest patient test of Wada 1997's hyperplasia prediction is EVOLVE's parathyroidectomy secondary endpoint (reported reduced in the full paper; not in the abstract I read). Worth citing in entry 2's judgement rather than leaving it only in entry 3.

Efficacy: Walter 2013 (PMID 23674604) is the etelcalcetide 5/6-Nx rat with 'reduced amounts of vascular calcification'; no patient calcification trial for etelcalcetide exists, so that prediction is untested, which the draft could state.
rule_questions: 1. Does a regulator's safety-margin sentence (on-target toxicity in animals at exposures close to clinical exposure) count as a dose/exposure-target comparison? I read dose as 'did the model-derived efficacious exposure hold in patients' and say no; the EMA sentence belongs in safety if anywhere.

2. Are EMA EPARs admissible under rule 1? The whitelist names FDA label/review, DOI, registry; an EPAR scientific discussion is the regulatory equivalent of an FDA review and should be added explicitly or excluded explicitly.

3. Applying the 'endpoints the model never modelled' precedent (HF/natriuretic peptides, #66), a null outcomes trial (EVOLVE) is not contra when the model had no outcomes endpoint. But the atlas then has no way to show that the hard-endpoint test happened and was null; a convention (judgement-only, or a new status) is needed. I could not read #66 (file access restricted), so I applied the precedent as described by the caller.

4. May one biomarker (PTH) carry both the engagement and the efficacy 'same' when the disease is defined by that biomarker? The draft does this with the same Block 2004 source; cf-cftr uses different sources for the two cells.

5. Direction matched but pre-specified primary missed (ADVANCE: Agatston P=0.073, volume P=0.009, authors say 'may attenuate'): is that 'same' with magnitude direction_only, or does a missed primary demand a stricter label? The brief's magnitude field cannot record 'primary missed'.
